tagline: Up the Rio Grande to Creede, then over the Divide.
intro: Out of South Fork, CO 149 follows the upper Rio Grande through the Rio Grande National Forest and comes in 21 miles to Creede. Past town it leaves the river, crosses the Continental Divide at Spring Creek Pass, 10,901 feet, and climbs again to Slumgullion Pass at 11,361 before it drops to Lake City and follows the Lake Fork down toward Blue Mesa Reservoir and US 50.

Both towns were silver camps. Creede went from 600 people to more than 10,000 in two years and kept its mines working until 1985. Lake City is where Alfred Packer was tried for murder and cannibalism, and the county museum there keeps buttons from the clothes of the men he ate.

moments.title: Wagon Wheel Gap
moments.text: In 1860 a miner in a hurry to get away from the Ute Colorow lost a wagon wheel in the Rio Grande here, and the wheel stayed in the mud.

moments.title: North Clear Creek Falls
moments.text: Half a mile off the highway on a paved county road, the creek pours over a deck of volcanic ash that hardened to rock some 27 million years ago.

moments.title: Slumgullion Earthflow
moments.text: The highway crosses a landslide that crawled down the valley about 700 years ago and dammed Lake San Cristobal, and a second flow still creeps over it about 23 feet a year.
